name: Customs Broker
title: Licensed Customs Broker
intro: From graduation to a customs broker licence under CBLR 2018: learn clearance on the job, apply when NACIN invites, pass the written and oral exams, then get the licence and practise.

phases.title: Graduate
phases.summary: Any stream; commerce, law or logistics helps.
points: You need a graduate degree, or a professional qualification or customs-clearance diploma that the Regulations accept.
Commerce helps with duties, invoices and accounts.
Law and logistics backgrounds also fit the work.

phases.title: Work in customs clearance
phases.summary: Many first work for a broker and learn on the job.
points: Clearance staff learn the work under a licensed broker.
Practical clearance experience makes passing the exam much easier.
Freight forwarders, shipping lines and import-export firms also hire clearance staff.

phases.title: Apply when NACIN invites
phases.summary: Through the Customs Commissionerate with jurisdiction.
points: Apply through your jurisdictional Customs Commissionerate.
Attempts are limited under the Regulations — prepare before you use one.

phases.title: Written and oral exams
phases.summary: An objective written exam on customs law and procedure, then an oral exam.
points: The written exam is objective, on customs law, tariff, procedures and allied laws; marks and pass rules are in the yearly notice.
Candidates who pass the written exam take an oral exam on practical clearance knowledge.
NACIN conducts the exam for CBIC under the Customs Brokers Licensing Regulations, 2018.

phases.title: Licence and practice
phases.summary: Meet the financial and fit-and-proper conditions, then run a brokerage or join a logistics firm.
points: The licence needs the financial and fit-and-proper conditions in the Regulations.
Licensed brokers earn fees per shipment; income grows with clients.
Growth path: clearance executive → licensed broker → own brokerage / logistics business; trade-compliance roles are related.
